segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Madam Tan. I'm Dr. Lim from the anesthesia team. I'll be looking after you during your surgery today. Let me go through some questions to make sure everything's in order, okay?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. I'm ready.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Can you tell me briefly why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I've been having bad stomach pains on the right side, especially after eating. The scans showed gallstones, so they want to remove the gallbladder laparoscopically.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Are you currently taking any medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes. I take combined oral contraceptive pills—ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone—every day. And I was on amoxicillin 500mg twice daily for a chest infection, but I stopped that two days ago as instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Do you have any allergies to medications, especially antibiotics like penicillin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, yes! I had a bad rash all over my body once when I took penicillin for a tooth infection. It was terrible, so I avoid all penicillin now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Important to know. Have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I had my last sip of water at 7 a.m., like the nurse instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Have you had any anesthesia before?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, once for a hernia repair. I woke up fine, just a bit sleepy. No problems at all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Lastly, are you able to carry out your daily activities without difficulty?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Mostly, lah. The gallbladder pains come and go, but I can still walk, climb stairs, and do housework unless it's a bad day.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Tan. We'll proceed with general anesthesia using a Laryngeal Mask Airway as planned. You'll get propofol and fentanyl for induction, sevoflurane for maintenance, and local anesthesia at the port sites. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I'm all set.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] fentanyl fifty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] LMA placed, no difficulty

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] 18-g IV in left hand, blood pressure cuff applied

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] normal saline two hundred fifty milliliters bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] blood pressure drop to eighty over fifty, treated with ephedrine ten milligrams IV

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] transient tachycardia to ninety, treated with fluid bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] sevoflurane started at two percent

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:25] bupivacaine ten milligrams at port sites

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I’m okay, just some pain at the incision sites, but it’s manageable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or vomiting since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit queasy, but not too bad. Haven’t eaten yet, though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any sore throat or difficulty breathing from the airway management?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: My throat’s a bit sore, like I’ve been shouting or something.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything from the operating room?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, everything’s a blur. One minute I was talking, next thing I know, I’m waking up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any other issues? Like dizziness, blurred vision, or anything else unusual?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Mouth’s really dry, but that’s about it. Oh, and my back’s a bit stiff from lying flat.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That’s normal. We’ll get you some water and monitor your vitals. You’re doing well for now.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thanks, doc. Appreciate it.
